title: Rotational Motion

sections.title: Moment of Inertia and the Parallel Axis Theorem
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Establish rotational inertia for discrete and continuous mass distributions and apply the parallel axis theorem rigorously through the center of mass.
unresolved_gaps: Lacks canonical worked examples for perpendicular axis theorem and continuous integration of standard planar bodies in current KB.
No verified canonical question atoms for standalone parallel axis theorem calculations in current staging.

sections.title: Torque and Fixed-Axis Rotational Dynamics
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Formulate the dynamical relation tau_net = I alpha for rigid bodies rotating about a fixed axis or accelerating through the center of mass.
source_references: University Physics with Modern Physics, 13th Edition.pdf
unresolved_gaps: Missing worked example demonstrating tau = I alpha for coupled pulley-mass systems.
Absence of verified canonical question atoms for fixed-axis rotational dynamics in current staging.

sections.title: Angular Momentum of a Particle About Fixed Reference Points
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Define angular momentum as a cross product L = r x p and deconstruct the misconception that rectilinear uniform or accelerated motion implies zero angular momentum.

sections.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum and Systems with Variable Inertia
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Analyze rotational systems under zero external torque, derive angular velocity scaling for variable mass distributions, and contrast angular momentum conservation with non-conservation of mechanical kinetic energy.

sections.title: Pure Rolling Kinematics and Energy Methods
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Connect translational and rotational kinematics under the non-slip constraint v_cm = R omega, analyze instantaneous center of rotation, and formulate combined kinetic energy.
unresolved_gaps: Pure rolling subtopic has no approved concept nodes, formula records, worked examples, or question atoms in ChapterSpec.
Need canonical atoms for rolling friction direction and acceleration on an inclined plane.

pedagogical_synthesis_notes: Mechanics Template: Progression follows structural hierarchy from rotational inertia (mass analog) to dynamics (tau = I alpha) to state quantities (L = r x p), culminating in conservation principles and variable inertia systems.

Scaffolded Progression: Section 3 and Section 4 leverage question ladder 'ladder-rot-ang-mom-01', taking students from single-particle trajectory angular momentum to complex two-body variable inertia conservation.

Misconception Disruption: Section 3 directly targets misc-rot-01 (straight-line motion having zero L), while Section 4 systematically breaks misc-rot-02 (mistaken assumption of kinetic energy conservation during radial mass redistribution).
unresolved_gaps: Gap in Topic 'moment-of-inertia': No canonical question atoms or worked examples currently staged for continuous mass integration or parallel/perpendicular axis theorem application.
Gap in Topic 'torque-and-rotation': Missing verified question atoms and worked examples for rotational equilibrium and fixed-axis dynamic torque problems (tau = I alpha).
Gap in Topic 'rolling-motion': Subtopic pure-rolling-kinematics in taxonomy references has zero approved concept placements, formulas, worked examples, or question atoms in the ChapterSpec.
Difficulty distribution gap: L4/L5 advanced synthesis questions (e.g. combined collision and rotation, rolling with sliding transition) are missing to satisfy top-percentile JEE Advanced preparation.
